The `source_x86_64` and `sha256sums_x86_64` arrays are declarative and do not trigger downloads or verifications during `makepkg --printsrcinfo`. The variables `pkgname`, `pkgver`, `arch`, `url`, `license`, `depends`, `provides`, `conflicts`, and `options` are all safely defined using static values or arrays. There is no evidence of malicious code execution, data exfiltration, or network activity during sourcing.

Since `makepkg --printsrcinfo` only parses the top-level metadata and does not execute the `package()` function or any other build-phase functions, the use of `ar`, `awk`, `bsdtar`, or `chmod` inside `package()` is irrelevant for this safety gate. These commands will not run during metadata parsing. The file adheres to standard AUR packaging practices and poses no risk during this specific operation.

No obfuscated code, dynamic payloads, or harmful top-level expressions are present. The PKGBUILD is safe to source for metadata extraction.
</details>
